body.text: Two courthouse doors opened on the same question in one afternoon: whether a permit — or a right — survives the drive across a state line.

A Georgia trucker's petition reached the Supreme Court in Johnson v. Jacobson (No. 26-255), asking whether Minnesota may switch his carry right off at the border. In Lawson v. Campbell, a federal judge in Boston refused to let Massachusetts moot a nonresident carry-delay case by issuing the permits late.

facts.title: 1. Johnson v. Jacobson — carry reciprocity reaches SCOTUS
2. United States v. Berger — "minimal registration is not an infringement"
3. Lawson v. Campbell — late permits do not moot the injury
